skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

version.changelog:
**User identity parameter handling is now fully automated and never exposed to users.**

- Identity (open-id) handling is moved to the system/scripts and is no longer collected from or shown to users.
- Updated SKILL.md: all user instructions, workflows, and usage examples now omit identity parameter prompts or exposure.
- Instructions strictly prohibit requesting or displaying internal user identifiers.
- Revised scripts and configuration references to support the new identity automation.
- More structured skill documentation and formatting improvements.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does the advertised pet-video analysis, but it silently manages user identity, creates or reuses local account state, stores tokens, and contacts a remote login service in ways users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Cloud video analysis and historical report retrieval fit the stated purpose, but the implementation also reads workspace identity state, silently creates or reuses a default user, calls a remote phoneLogin/register endpoint, and stores returned tokens in a local SQLite database without a clear user-facing privacy and retention explanation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md discloses cloud analysis, local attachment handling, and history queries, but it instructs identity handling to be internal and hidden from users; that under-discloses credential and account-linkage behavior even though it is not evidence of outright deception or exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation appears to be ordinary Python files plus declared dependencies; I did not find an installer, post-install hook, obfuscated loader, or automatic execution path outside the documented scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network upload of provided videos is proportionate to the service, but reading OPENCLAW-derived workspace identity files and persisting account credentials expands local and remote data exposure beyond what a typical video-analysis skill user would expect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill creates and updates a workspace data SQLite database and stores username, realname, email, token, and open_token fields; this persistence is purposeful for report association but high-impact and not sufficiently scoped or explained.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet drying-box videos or URLs to the Life Emergence remote service and letting the skill silently associate activity with an internal user identity. Before use, review how the service stores uploaded media, generated reports, local SQLite account data, and tokens, and avoid using it with sensitive customer, clinic, or household footage unless that data handling is acceptable.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr use is in a generic local DAO and is not evidence of code execution; it is a hardening issue if untrusted filter keys ever reach it, but it does not drive the verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: The scanner concern is partly supported: the skill uses local files, network calls, and identity state without a separate permissions boundary, and that matters because credentials and account state are involved.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported in part: identity bootstrap, local default-user creation, workspace identity reads, and silent remote login/register behavior go beyond the narrow video-analysis surface and are under-disclosed.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Historical report listing and export links are documented, but local storage of identity and token fields and generic CRUD helpers create broader sensitive-data exposure than the user-facing purpose explains.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger rules are documented and require video/report intent, but automatic history lookup on keywords can still surprise users because it reaches cloud account history.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Remote upload of provided media is expected and disclosed at a high level, but retention, local saved-file lifecycle, credential storage, and possible debug logging are not adequately explained.
[E1] unexpected: External requests are expected for analysis, but sending an implicitly resolved identity to a remote login/register endpoint is a material concern because the account-linkage flow is not clearly presented to users.
[OH1] expected: The cited subprocess path is commented out and I did not find active shell execution from model output; this finding is not supported as a material issue.
[P2] expected: A zero-width character exists in SKILL.md, but I did not find hidden operational instructions attached to it, so this is a cleanliness issue rather than proof of malicious prompt injection.
[YR4] expected: The metadata-poisoning match appears to be caused by the same invisible character near manifest text; I did not find offensive tooling or exploit content.
